Values
Southbury Whole School Core Values
At Southbury we are committed to helping our pupils become knowledgeable, independent and positive members of the school, local and global community.
One of the many ways we encourage this is through our whole school Values which are linked closely to our shared British Values.
The key value changes on a half termly basis and is covered daily across the curriculum, through discussion and in assemblies.
They are key to the social, intellectual, emotional, spiritual and moral development of the whole child. We encourage children to consider these values, and thereby to develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes that enable them to develop as reflective learners and grow to be emotionally intelligent, educated and civilised adults.

Welcome
As Headteacher, it is my pleasure to warmly welcome you to Southbury Primary School's website.
Southbury is a happy and successful multicultural two-form entry primary school, built in 1905 and situated in Enfield. As a school, we are extremely proud to reflect the cultural and ethnic diversity of the area we serve.
Our school vision is very simple but of fundamental importance to us all. We want all of our staff and parents/carers to work together to enable all the children who pass through the school to reach their full potential in a safe, happy and caring environment. Our school motto is 'Dream Big, Fly High' and that is our wish for our children.
We want our pupils to leave Southbury confident that they will be able to succeed in secondary school and beyond. Ultimately, we hope that they will be lifelong learners who will be able to find employment that they enjoy doing and is meaningful and rewarding for them as they continue with their journeys through life. To achieve this, it is crucial they have the best possible start to school life and that is what we aim to give them at Southbury.
The school has been very successful over the years and as a staff, we constantly strive to offer the pupils at Southbury the best possible education. We are proud to deliver an exciting and enriching curriculum, as well as lots of real-life experiences that will provide children with a range of knowledge and skills. We are proud of our school and what we can offer and would warmly welcome anyone interested in sending their child to attend Southbury to come along and see us in action. If you would like to book a viewing of the school, please contact us via the school office and we will gladly book you in.

French
Bonjour! Comment ça va?
At Southbury Primary School, we are proud of the many languages already spoken in our community and we build on this by providing pupils with the opportunity to learn another language. In KS2, the teaching of a modern foreign language is compulsory under the 2014 curriculum. KS2 pupils learn French and have a weekly lesson and as of September 2023, pupils are following the Language Angels scheme of work. This is an exciting scheme which provides children with strong foundations in French. Children receive logins, so they can practise language covered in class through games and songs online to consolidate their language learning at home.

PE and Sports Premium
PE and Sport at Southbury Primary School
At Southbury, we believe PE and sport are an important part of every child’s education. We make sure that all children take part in at least two hours of physical activity each week as part of the school day.
We know that taking part in sport and physical activity helps children stay healthy, build confidence, and learn important life skills like teamwork, fair play, and respect for others.
In 2013 - 2026, the government introduced special funding (called the PE and Sport Premium) to help schools improve their PE and sports provision. This money was given to all state-funded schools with primary-aged children.
At Southbury, we used this funding in a number of ways to give our pupils the best possible experiences in PE and sport:
Providing 'active lunchtimes' where qualified PE coaches lead a variety of games and activities with the children.
Taking part in local sports tournaments, festivals, and competitions for children of all ages.
Entering children into leagues and competitions run by the Enfield PE Team.
Using ICT in PE lessons, so children can watch and evaluate their own performances and those of their classmates. This also helps teachers track progress and plan next steps.
Hiring qualified sports coaches to teach a variety of sports during PE lessons.
We’re proud to offer a wide range of physical activities at Southbury and are committed to helping every child enjoy being active and develop a love for sport that lasts a lifetime.

PSHE & SRE
PSHE at Southbury Primary School
Dream Big, Fly High.
At Southbury Primary School, we believe that education is about more than academic achievement. We want every child to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to understand themselves, build positive relationships, make informed choices and contribute positively to the world around them.
Our PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) curriculum plays an important part in helping children to become confident, respectful, resilient and responsible young people who are ready to flourish both now and in the future.
Our PSHE journey reflects our school motto:
Dream Big – developing a strong sense of self, building confidence and resilience, managing emotions, developing positive relationships, showing kindness and empathy, celebrating diversity and believing in our own potential.
Fly High – becoming increasingly independent, communicating effectively, learning to resolve conflict, making informed and safe choices, taking responsibility and being ready for the opportunities and challenges of the wider world.
What do children learn in PSHE?
Our curriculum is organised around three interconnected strands. These areas are revisited throughout a child's time at Southbury, allowing knowledge and understanding to develop and deepen as children get older.
❤️ Health and Wellbeing
Children learn how to look after their physical, mental and emotional health and wellbeing.

A carefully planned and progressive curriculum
PSHE is taught through weekly lessons, with learning organised into half-termly units. Our curriculum follows a spiral approach, meaning that important ideas and concepts are revisited at different ages, with children's understanding becoming increasingly detailed and sophisticated as they progress through the school.
In Nursery and Reception, PSHE learning forms part of our Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSED) curriculum. This provides an important foundation for the learning children continue to develop throughout Key Stages 1 and 2.
Across Years 1–6, children follow a planned sequence of themes:
This progression enables children to revisit key themes while encountering new knowledge, vocabulary and increasingly complex ideas as they mature.
How is PSHE taught?
PSHE lessons provide opportunities for children to talk, listen, think, question, reflect and apply their learning to real-life situations.
Lessons may include:
Teachers adapt learning to meet the needs and developmental stage of their pupils. We place particular importance on creating a safe, supportive and respectful environment where children feel comfortable asking questions and expressing their ideas.
Our PSHE learning does not happen only during timetabled lessons. The messages and values explored in PSHE are reinforced through our school values, assemblies, collective worship, enrichment opportunities, visits, visitors and everyday life at Southbury.

Equality, diversity and respect
At Southbury, we want every child to feel safe, valued and respected.
Our PSHE curriculum reflects the diverse families, cultures, backgrounds and experiences within our school and wider society. Children learn about equality, fairness, respect and the importance of treating others with kindness and dignity.
As children progress through the school, they develop their understanding of diversity and learn to recognise and challenge stereotypes, discrimination and prejudice.
We believe that celebrating difference helps children to develop empathy, understanding and a strong sense of belonging.
Keeping children safe
Safeguarding is at the heart of our PSHE curriculum.
Children learn how to recognise potential risks, make informed choices, keep themselves safe and identify trusted adults who can help them. Online safety and responsible use of technology are also an important part of our learning.
Some PSHE topics are sensitive. These are taught carefully, objectively and in an age-appropriate way, taking account of children's developmental needs and respecting the diversity of families, cultures and beliefs.
Children are never expected to share personal experiences during PSHE lessons. Instead, we create a safe environment where children can discuss scenarios, ask questions and develop the knowledge and confidence to seek help when they need it.
For Parents/Carers
We recognise that parents and carers are children's first educators, and we value the important role families play in supporting children's personal development.

Children may sometimes have questions following a PSHE lesson. We encourage parents and carers to listen, answer questions honestly and sensitively, and reassure children that it is always okay to ask for help.

What about Relationships and Sex Education?
Relationships Education and Health Education form part of the statutory primary curriculum, alongside relevant learning within Science.
At Southbury, we currently do not teach additional non-statutory Sex Education beyond the statutory requirements for primary-aged children. Consequently, there are currently no planned lessons from which parents need to withdraw their children.
For further information, please see our PSHE Policy and Parent Information and FAQs.
Our PSHE vocabulary
Developing children's vocabulary is an important part of our PSHE curriculum. As children move through the school, they encounter and use increasingly sophisticated language to help them talk about their health, emotions, relationships, rights, responsibilities and the wider world.
Our PSHE and Citizenship Vocabulary Progression sets out the key vocabulary children will encounter across different themes and stages of their learning.

Governors
The role of a school Governor is to help with the smooth running of the school and ensuring that the school is doing everything it can to provide a safe and nurturing environment for all pupils.
The Governing Body: roles, responsibilities and organisation
Southbury has a Governing Body who holds the school to account. Governors are made up from various groups; teachers, non-teaching staff, parents, people from the local community and representatives from the local authority. Together they meet every term and discuss raising academic standards, ensuring the school offers good value for money within a safe and secure environment and discuss key issues relating to the school. These include the implementation of governor initiatives, pupil progress, academic standards and all matters relating to the school's finance premises.
School governors are ordinary people from the local community, who wish to make a positive contribution to children’s education. They are the largest volunteer force in the country. All maintained schools in England have a Governing Body. It is responsible for overseeing many of the strategic decisions of the school and has an important part to play in raising school standards through acting as a ‘critical friend’ - supporting, challenging and asking questions.
The Governing Body’s three key roles are:
Schools need governors with a range of skills and interests, so almost anyone can become a school governor. New governors receive training and support from the school, the Local Authority and other governors. If you are interested in assisting our school in this way, please contact the office for further details.
Organisation of the Governing Body The Governing Body works in close partnership with the Headteacher, staff and the Local Authority. Whilst the Headteacher is responsible for the day-to-day running of the school, the governors are involved with strategic matters.
Southbury School has two sub-committees, which meet termly:
Small groups of governors (panels) are involved with matters such as appointing a Headteacher, staff grievances and formal complaints procedures; while some individual governors have responsibilities for specific areas within the school, for example safeguarding, Pupil Premium or GDPR (data protection).

Maths at Southbury
Curriculum Aims and Intent
At Southbury Primary School, we aim to develop mathematicians who have a foundation for understanding number, reasoning, thinking logically and problem-solving with resilience. In line with the National Curriculum Objectives for Mathematics, our curriculum is designed to engage and challenge, whilst meeting the needs of all pupils.
Our intent is for all pupils to:
Through careful progression planning and sequencing, we aim to ensure that all children have equal access to a broad and balanced curriculum that enhances life experiences for all.
Our mathematics curriculum provides children with the opportunity to apply their learning in different contexts, such as science and technology, embedding and consolidating skills. This love of learning and depth of knowledge is promoted across the school. Our core values underpin everything that we do and support our aspirations and ambitions for all our pupils.
Our curriculum leader, Carly Cinotti, leads Mathematics. The role of the curriculum leader is key to the implementation of our curriculum. They are responsible for the whole school approach to Mathematics and have oversight of progress from EYFS through to Year 6. They attend network meetings, internal and external CPD and have the knowledge, expertise and practical skills to be able to lead mathematics effectively. Mathematics is regularly reviewed (through weekly subject leader time) and to ensure it is being implemented effectively and coverage and breadth and balance is planned for.

Music
Overview of class lessons
Music is taught across the whole school using the Charanga scheme of work. We have a Musician of the Month focus and the children are exposed to music by this musician every week and learn a few simple facts about them too. Everyone learns to sing and enjoys our Key Stage singing assemblies each week.
We have good links with Enfield Music Services who come in across the year to work with different age groups, their specialist teachers extend beyond our existing provision in school. Children are given an opportunity to 'perform' to the rest of the school and their parents through this at the end of the block, as well as performing in the Early Years, KS1 Nativities and the Year 6 end of year production.
Nursery: In Nursery, we sing lots of songs including nursery rhymes, counting songs and movement songs. We use a variety of instruments so that we can gain confidence using them, learn correct techniques and learn about rhythm.
Reception: Reception builds on the work done in Nursery, continuing to build children’s confidence in finding their singing voices and playing percussion instruments and to extend their song repertoire. They start to improvise and to use pictures to represent sounds.
Year 1: During year 1 we continue to learn new songs and also play instruments such as drums, tambourines, woodblocks and triangles, exploring the different sounds and creating patterns as well as playing to a steady beat. We are also introduced to glockenspiels to explore using pitched instruments.
Year 2: By year 2 the children are becoming confident singers and can cope well with simple rhythm work. They have the opportunity to compose as a whole class and in small groups using classroom instruments and to represent their sounds with symbols.
Year 3: Children in year 3 are usually able to sing in tune and to cope with more complex rhythmic work. As their reading skills improve, they are able to learn songs quickly and to accompany them on instruments. They compose in small groups using tuned and untuned percussion instruments.
Year 4: During year 4 we continue to learn more complex songs and learn accompanying musical parts to play alongside the songs.
Year 5: By year 5 the children have learnt good singing techniques and are able to sing songs in two parts and to look at more complex accompaniments using instruments. They will also use tuned and untuned instruments creatively as they compose in groups.
Year 6: By the time children reach the top of the school they are familiar with a range of songs in a variety of styles and are familiar with many tuned and untuned instruments. They will have the opportunity to compose songs and raps and to create and notate longer compositions.

Admissions
Southbury School is a Community School, therefore our admissions, including in-year admissions, are dealt with by the Local Authority (Enfield Council), in accordance with their admissions criteria.
For more information, please visit: www.enfield.gov.uk/admissions
Click here to read our admissions criteria
Applying for a Nursery place at Southbury
We offer Nursery places from two years old. We also have a limited number of 30 hour spaces for eligible children. As our Nursery sessions run from 8.30-11.30am and 12-3pm, those who are eligible for the 30 hours of funding are asked to pay £15 per week to cover the additional 2.5 hours they are with us across the week. If a parent/carer would prefer not to pay for these additional hours then there is the option of collecting your child at 11.30am then returning them at 12pm for the next session. If you would like to book a Nursery tour for 2026-2027 admissions, or request more information about funding and places, please contact the school office by calling 0208 804 1710 or emailing office@southbury.enfield.sch.uk
Applying for a Primary place at Southbury
If you would like to apply for a space at our school, you can apply online at www.eadmissions.org.uk
For all other admissions queries contact the Enfield Admissions Service:
